title: Chapter 9 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of NgModules, feature modules, Shared/Core patterns, and standalone components.

questions.question: What is the purpose of NgModule in Angular?
options: To group related components, directives, pipes, and services
questions.explanation: NgModule is a compilation context that organizes related code.

questions.question: Which array in @NgModule lists the components, directives, and pipes that belong to the module?
questions.explanation: `declarations` is where you list the view classes that belong to this module.

questions.question: How do you make a component in a module available to other modules?
options: Declare it and list it in the `exports` array.
Import it directly in the other module.
Use a service to share it.
questions.explanation: A component must be both declared and exported to be public.

questions.question: A component can be declared in more than one NgModule.
questions.explanation: A component can only belong to one module. Duplicate declarations cause an error.

questions.question: Which array in the root module identifies the root component?
questions.explanation: `bootstrap` is used only in the root module to launch the root component.

questions.question: What CLI command creates a new feature module?
questions.explanation: `ng generate module my-module` (or `ng g m my-module`) scaffolds a new module.

questions.question: Which method should feature modules use for routing?
questions.explanation: Feature and lazy‑loaded modules use `forChild()` to add routes without re‑initializing the router.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of a SharedModule?
options: To re‑export common components, directives, and pipes.
questions.explanation: SharedModule collects frequently used items and re‑exports them for other modules.

questions.question: Where should app‑wide singleton services be provided?
questions.explanation: CoreModule is the recommended place for singleton services imported only in AppModule.

questions.question: A CoreModule should be imported in every feature module.
questions.explanation: CoreModule should be imported only once in AppModule to keep services singletons.

questions.question: A CoreModule often includes a constructor guard using `@Optional()` and `@SkipSelf()` to prevent ____ imports.
questions.explanation: The guard throws an error if the module is imported more than once.

questions.question: What is the purpose of `forRoot()` pattern in a module?
options: To provide an alternate version of the module
To configure singleton services when the module is imported once
questions.explanation: `forRoot()` returns the module with providers, ensuring services are singletons.

questions.question: What does `standalone: true` signify?
options: The component cannot be used with routing.
The component does not need to be declared in an NgModule.
questions.explanation: A standalone component is self‑contained and does not belong to any module.

questions.question: Which method bootstraps an application without an AppModule?
questions.explanation: `bootstrapApplication()` is the new function for bootstrapping standalone components.

questions.question: You can import an NgModule into a standalone component's `imports` array.
questions.explanation: Standalone components can import existing NgModules seamlessly.

questions.question: How do you provide a router to a standalone bootstrapped app?
options: By using `provideRouter(routes)` in the bootstrap providers
By importing RouterModule in the AppComponent
questions.explanation: `provideRouter()` is the standalone way to configure routing.

questions.question: Can you mix standalone components and NgModules in the same Angular app?
questions.explanation: Angular fully supports mixing both approaches.

questions.question: The Angular CLI (v17+) generates components with `standalone: true` by default.
questions.explanation: Starting with v17, standalone is the default for new components.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of lazy‑loading a feature module?
options: It makes the module easier to write.
It improves initial load time by loading the module only when needed.
It reduces the number of components.
questions.explanation: Lazy loading defers fetching code until the route is activated, speeding up startup.

questions.question: Which NgModule array is used to register services at the module level?
questions.explanation: `providers` registers services with the module's injector.
